evidence_detail: CHEMISTRY/PHYSICS VERDICT: 36.1 is physically plausible but is NOT the better-supported of the two values, and this row carries the weaker provenance of the pair. (1) Phase is physical: gamma-valerolactone (GVL, CAS 108-29-2) melts at -31 C / 244 K and boils at 207-208 C / 480-481 K (PubChem CID 7921 experimental, NTP 1992); at 298.15 K it is a liquid over a 236 K window, so a liquid-phase static permittivity is physically realisable and the phase assignment is sound. (2) Magnitude is physical: GBL (the C4 homologue) has a measured static eps = 41.64 at 298.15 K (ThermoML 10.1021/je900503p, Dekameter, U=0.06 at 95%); GVL has one more CH2 (molar volume 95.4 vs 76.6 cm3/mol) so its number density is 0.80x GBL, and a Kirkwood-Froehlich estimate with the repository's own xTB dipoles (mu_GVL=5.038 D vs mu_GBL=4.936 D, ratio 1.02) gives eps_GVL = 34.9 at g=1.0, spanning 31.5-38.2 for g=0.90-1.10. Both 36.1 and 36.9 fall inside that band, so chemistry cannot discriminate them; the lactone family brackets eps(298 K) at 35-42. (3) The 2.2% spread is NOT inter-laboratory reproducibility: 0.8/36.1 = 2.22%, which exceeds the project's own 2.00% relative tolerance by 1.11x, but the real point is that 2.2% is far SMALLER than the reproducibility actually documented for static permittivity of this exact compound class. The same ThermoML GBL file reports two replicates at 293.15 K (42.34 and 42.81) differing by 0.47 = 1.10%, i.e. 8x its own stated U=0.06, and the literature value commonly quoted for GBL (39.1) differs from the primary 41.64 by 6.1%. A 2.2% gap is therefore within the NOISE of this quantity and is not evidence of a transcription error or a different physical quantity. (4) Both CAN be correct on one eps(T) curve: the measured homologue slope is d(eps)/dT = -0.129 /K (GBL, 293-313 K), so a 0.8 gap corresponds to only 6.2 K (at the local 298-303 K slope of -0.108 /K, 7.4 K). 36.9 at 291.9 K (18.8 C) and 36.1 at 298.15 K lie on the SAME line, and a 25 C vs 20 C labelling difference alone reproduces 81% of the gap. Neither leg reports a temperature: this row's T=298.15 K is flagged temperature_source=review_table_standard_room_temperature, i.e. an ASSUMED standard room temperature, not a reported one, and the 36.9 leg is flagged temperature_source=not_reported. The apparent same-temperature conflict is an artefact of the ingest assigning 298.15 K to two documents that never stated a temperature. (5) Water content: 1.8 wt% H2O would add about +0.8 to eps (linear bound against eps_H2O=78.2), so a small purity difference can also produce the gap in the same direction. DECISION RATIONALE: HOLD rather than PASS because the row has zero contributing observations (ledger search for GAEKPEKOJKCEMS-UHFFFAOYSA-N returns 0 rows), condition_pair_valid=false, NO_BAND_OBSERVATIONS_FOUND, and its 298.15 K is a constructed review-table assumption rather than a reported measurement condition; HOLD rather than FAIL because 36.1 is chemically and physically sound and the review table is a legitimate secondary source. RETAIN_PARALLEL is recommended over choosing a primary because the two values are the same physical quantity within measurement noise, are not independent replications (no primary measurement exists for either), and the 2.2% gap is smaller than the documented spread of the method itself; rejecting either would discard real information and averaging is forbidden by project rule.

CHEMISTRY/PHYSICS VERDICT: 36.9 is marginally the more plausible of the two numbers and is the better-sourced leg, but it is not established as a 298.15 K value and must not be promoted to primary on this evidence. (1) Phase is physical: GVL is a liquid at 298.15 K, mp -31 C (244 K) and bp 207-208 C (480-481 K) per PubChem CID 7921 experimental (NTP 1992); density 1.047-1.054 g/cm3. A liquid-phase static permittivity is realisable with a 236 K liquid window, so the phase assignment is sound. (2) Magnitude: the lactone homology brackets eps(298 K) between GBL (measured 41.64 at 298.15 K, ThermoML 10.1021/je900503p) and the Kirkwood-Froehlich prediction for GVL of 34.9 at g=1.0 (band 31.5-38.2 for g=0.90-1.10 using the repo's xTB dipoles 5.038 D vs 4.936 D and the 0.80x number-density ratio). 36.9 sits near the centre of that band and is the value returned by the live Reaxys index for this substance (probes/reaxys_core_four_crosscheck.csv, location 'supporting information', Segato et al. 2021 Inorg. Chim. Acta 522 120372), and Reaxys holds exactly ONE dielectric row for GVL in the entire substance record. Slight edge to 36.9 over 36.1: the higher value is the one consistent with a normal-purity dry sample read at or slightly below room temperature, and 36.9 is what an independent curated index reproduces, whereas 36.1 exists only as a review-table transcription. (3) The 2.2% gap (0.8/36.1) exceeds the project's 2.00% relative tolerance by 1.11x but is well inside the method's real reproducibility: the primary GBL file carries two replicates at one temperature differing by 1.10% (8x its stated U=0.06), and the commonly quoted GBL value 39.1 differs from the primary 41.64 by 6.1%. So 2.2% is noise, not a transcription error, and not a finite-frequency artefact: the primary GBL comparison was made at zero frequency (ePropName 'Relative permittivity at zero frequency') and both GVL legs are low-frequency/static claims. (4) Both can be simultaneously correct: with d(eps)/dT = -0.129 /K measured on the homologue, the 0.8 gap equals 6.2 K of temperature. 36.9 at 291.9 K (18.8 C) and 36.1 at 298.15 K are the same curve. Critically, this leg reports NO temperature at all (temperature_source=not_reported; the Reaxys row 'has no temperature column at all' per reports/reaxys_core_four_crosscheck.md section 3.3), so its T=298.15 K is an ingest assumption, not a measurement condition, and the 'same temperature' premise of the conflict is unsupported for this leg. Water content is the other legitimate route: about 1.8 wt% H2O raises eps by ~+0.8 (eps_H2O=78.2), so a wetter sample reads high, i.e. toward 36.9, not away from it. (5) The 4th data point argues for caution: the Perricone 2011 thesis Tableau 8 gives 32 at 25 C and elsewhere 34 (reports/g1plus_perricone_thesis_crosscheck.md), which is 11.4% BELOW 36.1 and far outside any rounding or temperature explanation (that would need about 32 K of offset). That widens the true spread of GVL's literature eps to 32-36.9 and shows the field has not converged, so neither of these two rows may be declared the canonical value. DECISION RATIONALE: HOLD because provenance is incomplete (zero contributing observations; ledger search for GAEKPEKOJKCEMS-UHFFFAOYSA-N returns 0 rows), condition_pair_valid=false, NO_BAND_OBSERVATIONS_FOUND, and the 298.15 K is an assumption over a source that explicitly reports no temperature; HOLD rather than FAIL because 36.9 is physically sound, is the only dielectric number the Reaxys index holds for this compound, and comes from a primary-article supporting information rather than a review. RETAIN_PARALLEL over RETAIN_AS_PRIMARY: designating this leg primary would silently assert a temperature the source does not state and would bury the unresolved 32/34 legs; the pair should stand side by side until a temperature-resolved primary measurement is read.
